newsitem.title: CHINA: China power problems seen hitting aluminium output.
newsitem.headline: China power problems seen hitting aluminium output.

text.p: Energy shortages in China are hitting aluminium smelters and will limit growth of output to just 1.7 percent in 1996, a British researcher said in a report at a metals conference on Tuesday.

"The power problems being encountered by the Chinese smelters should ensure that output for the full year is only marginally higher than in the previous year," Metal Bulletin Research senior metals analyst Raju Daswani said in the report.
China's aluminium production was expected to be nearly 1.7 million tonnes this year, not enough to meet rising demand, the report said.
China would have an aluminium deficit of about 200,000 tonnes over the next few years and would likely be a net importer of the metal to the year 2000, it said.
Demand was seen rising by just 1.6 percent in 1996 but that figure would grow from 1997, it said.
"Although there are various plans...to increase capacity and overall utilisation levels, increases in output are likely to be matched by equivalent rises in demand," it said.
Aluminium production would see greater increases as energy problems were solved and smelter capacity was boosted, it said but gave no further details.
China's aluminium output slipped 1.66 percent in the first six months to 806,300 tonnes from the year-ago period, official figures show.
Imports of unwrought aluminium and alloys rose a year-on-year 19.5 percent in the first half to 180,500 tonnes.
Official forecasts have said aluminium output would top 1.8 million tonnes in 1996, 10 percent more than 1995's official estimated output of 1.65 million tonnes.
